races.name: Tote Guarantee Never Beaten By SP Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Concert Party
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has finished no better than fourth in her last four, with zero wins or places on similar Going over comparable trips — her 9-length defeat last time at Good (12f) offers little encouragement, and she looks likely to be racing closer to the pace than she wants given the field's make-up.|
runners_data.comment: Concert Party was a winner three starts back, and again four starts back, before finishing ninth last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a useful rating keeps her right amongst the leading dangers despite that below-par finish.

runners_data.name: Jr Mahon
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by nature but with four hold-up rivals in the same field he will be pushed into a midfield berth he rarely uses; trainer Ian Donoghue has a 0/9 recent strike rate and he has managed only one place from ten similar-going runs, making his task difficult wherever he settles.|
runners_data.comment: Jr Mahon has been no better than fourth in five starts and remains winless in that sequence, but returns after a 38-day break having run over today's trip and going before. A rating well clear of his official mark of 63 makes him a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's yard is in 2/23 form and this horse has two wins and two places from 13 similar-going runs, giving her the most solid Good-ground record among the hold-up brigade; she comes into this fresh (13 days) and if the pace unravels late she is among the most likely to capitalise.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back, and again five starts back, Kashel Spring was only fifth last time out but has run over today's trip and going before. Racing off a 77 official mark, the pair of recent wins make her a leading danger.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, she is on a two-timer at Good (both over shorter 8f) and steps up sharply in trip — her ability to see out 9f at a controlled gallop is the central question of the race, but no rival is capable of pressuring her early and she sets this race entirely on her own terms.|
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, and again two starts back, Minaun View followed that with an eighth three starts back in a mixed six-race sample. She has run over today's going before, and a rating of 67 keeps her right in this despite the inconsistency.

runners_data.name: Macinamillion
runners_data.note: A prominent-travelling type with stamina proven over 18f-20f on Good ground (one win at each), making him the most credible stayer in the prominent group — the 284-day absence is a major concern for Raymond Hurley's yard (0/0 T14), however, and fitness must be questioned.|
runners_data.comment: Macinamillion was a winner three starts back and third four starts back, but his last two starts before a 284-day absence both ended unplaced. He has run over today's going before, and a modest rating of 55 leaves questions fresh off such a lengthy break.

runners_data.name: May Night
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old natural hold-up horse who, with a year off the track, will be short of peak fitness — she tends to race in rear and her historical Good-ground best has come over shorter trips; her redistribution into midfield only compounds an already limited chance.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out but that was 364 days ago, May Night is winless in this sequence which also featured two unplaced efforts. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating well clear of his 57 official mark hints at more back from a lengthy break.

runners_data.name: Talking Tough
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and a hold-up runner by inclination, this 9-year-old's recent form figures of 0-6-0-8-7 tell a bleak story; forced into a midfield berth here by field dynamics, his finishing propensity to drop away makes him one of the least interesting runners in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Talking Tough has not finished better than sixth in his last five starts and remains winless throughout. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a strong speed figure offers a shred of encouragement, but on the placings alone he is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: She's Ideal
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's yard is active (3/21 T14) and she races prominently, the natural position to be in if Minaun View sets a moderate tempo — she has placed at 10f on Good ground and is fit from a run nine days ago, making her the most credible established rival to the leader.|
runners_data.comment: She's Ideal was runner-up six starts back, but her form has since dipped to two sevenths and an eighth in her last three starts. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 62 leaves her with more to prove.

runners_data.name: Battling Siki
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who showed his best effort of late with a third over 12f on Good ground (2 of 5 sim-going runs in the frame) — fitted with a hood, he is a more intriguing latecomer than most, but the low tempo means he will need something to go wrong up front to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Battling Siki was third last time out and has been competitive without getting the breaks in this sequence, though yet to score. He has run over today's going before, and a rating well clear of his 69 official mark makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Romantic War
runners_data.note: A fader at the finish by pattern and a hold-up type shunted into midfield by force of numbers — form figures of 30-090 on going to soft/heavy predominantly, and a 86-day absence for a yard with 0/0 recent wins make this a very difficult each-way proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Romantic War's only placed effort in this sequence was third five starts back, and he remains winless with three unplaced runs since. Fit again after an 86-day break, he has run over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 43 leaves him with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Shelbourne Flyer
runners_data.note: Trained by Noel Meade (1/13 T14) and genuine in hold-up/rear roles by nature, his best effort this year was a second over 7f on Good — step up to 9f is untested and being squeezed into midfield rather than his preferred rearward position leaves him racing without his natural tactical comfort.|
runners_data.comment: Shelbourne Flyer's best effort was a runner-up spot five starts back, but he remains winless with little else to shout about in this sequence. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 55 puts him among the outsiders here.

races.paceDynamic: Minaun View is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, having won twice recently over shorter trips at Good, will look to dictate from the outset at a tempo that suits her own stamina limitations — with no obvious challenger for the lead, she is likely to control the fractions and set a sustainable, even gallop. She's Ideal and Macinamillion are the only other horses with genuine prominent-running profiles and will look to track Minaun View closely, creating a small lead group but no burning pace. The majority of this field — Concert Party, Kashel Spring, Battling Siki, Jr Mahon, May Night, Talking Tough, Romantic War and Shelbourne Flyer — are natural hold-up or midfield types, but there are far more of them than the race shape can accommodate at the back; Jr Mahon, May Night, Shelbourne Flyer, Romantic War and Talking Tough are the most likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than they would ideally prefer, scrambling for positions in the middle of the field. With one front-runner setting a controlled tempo over 1m1½f on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently behind Minaun View and produce a sustained finishing effort — genuine hold-up horses launching late runs will be disadvantaged by the lack of a strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Minaun View Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Minaun View makes all unchallenged and the pace stays moderate, allowing her to dictate every yard.
scenarios.body: Minaun View has won her last two on Good ground and steps up in trip, but a controlled pace over 9f could see her stamina hold sufficiently if she settles well; She's Ideal and Macinamillion, tracking prominently, are best positioned to pick up any weakness but may lack the class to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Wear Her Down
scenarios.trigger: If Minaun View's stamina is tested as She's Ideal or Macinamillion press her from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A sustained tempo in the final three furlongs stretches the front-runner and a prominent-travelling horse with better staying credentials swoops to lead close home; Macinamillion won over 1m6f on Good and has the stamina profile, while She's Ideal has placed at this trip on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Lucky Bounce
scenarios.trigger: If Minaun View overcooks the pace or tires sharply, creating a rare gap for a hold-up horse to close into.
scenarios.body: A genuine hold-up runner would need an unusually fast early tempo to produce their best, and while the fractions could collapse in the final furlong if Minaun View overextends, this scenario requires conditions that are unlikely given the lone leader's tendency to control rather than burn; Kashel Spring, who won twice on Good at this sort of trip, and Battling Siki are best suited if this narrow opportunity emerges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos As Pushed-Back Types Interfere
scenarios.trigger: If redistributed hold-up horses forced prominent are unsettled and create a tactical muddle, disrupting the flow of the race.
scenarios.body: Multiple horses racing out of their natural position in mid-pack could cause bumping or traffic issues in the home straight, with the race becoming messy and unpredictable; if the shape breaks down entirely, a horse with tactical versatility like Kashel Spring, who has won on Good ground and can be ridden with some flexibility, could benefit from the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View's stamina is unproven beyond 8f — watch whether she shortens stride or idles in the final two furlongs, as any wobble could open the door for She's Ideal or Macinamillion who are poised directly behind her.

Macinamillion's fitness after 284 days off is a significant unknown — if he shows signs of blowing or pulling up early, the prominent group loses its most experienced stayer and the race shape around Minaun View becomes even more one-dimensional.

With Jr Mahon, May Night, Talking Tough, Romantic War and Shelbourne Flyer all natural hold-up types forced into midfield positions, watch for scrimmaging or traffic problems on the home turn that could shut in Battling Siki or Kashel Spring if they attempt to improve late.

Concert Party, carrying 136lbs under Alan Casey (7lb claim), is the joint top-weight among the rear-runners — note whether she is given a patient ride or pushed forward early, as the jockey's positioning in the first furlong will determine whether she can realistically land a late run at all.

runners_data.name: Half Cut
runners_data.note: A 5-year-old with a concerning form string of 0-9 on most recent starts, this is a natural hold-up horse whose finishing tendency to fade makes it hard to fancy even if it navigates a midfield berth out of redistribution; trainer Anthony Mullins has had just one winner from four in the past 14 days and the 13-day turnaround gives no obvious fitness edge.|

runners_data.name: Tyraxes
runners_data.note: Denis Gerard Hogan's 4-year-old has been busy (6 days since last run, trip-and-pace headgear), showing a mix of reasonable efforts and poor finishes at shorter trips on Good; at heart a hold-up type now mapping to midfield, the step up to 1m1½f is a new question and three out of ten Good-going runs have placed without a win.|

runners_data.name: Taj Crown
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter, trained by K J Condon and ridden by W J Lee, who posted two placed efforts on Good ground in his history; with no rival to push him for the lead, he gets an uncontested role at his own pace which is the key race-shape advantage — his [STYLE_FIT] flag is a reminder he is operating as front-runner rather than prominent type, but the lack of competition makes it workable.|

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's 3-year-old showed a placed effort at 8f on Good and steps up in trip here; with an unresolved style profile, Ronan Whelan can find whatever position he likes off a single pace-setter, and the step to 1m1½f on consistent Good ground is a positive pointer for a horse who placed over 8f.|

runners_data.name: Countertop
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old with a deeply uninspiring form string of 0700-0, including a fade pattern flagged in the data; Michael Mulvany's runner is a true hold-up horse crammed into a midfield slot in this shape, and the lack of any placed effort on Good ground across five attempts makes it difficult to build a case.|

runners_data.name: Noble Venture
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge partners this Ms Sheila Lavery-trained 3-year-old who is very lightly raced with just two starts, finishing 10th and 7th; the trip looks stretched for current form, but the unknown ceiling keeps a small wildcard element alive on Good ground.|

runners_data.name: Shay's Dream
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien (T14: 19/58, strong strike rate), which is the principal angle here; the form reads 0-0-0 with a fade flag and no placing, and even a strong jockey booking needs something to work with over 1m1½f in a genuine maiden.|

runners_data.name: Stabannon
runners_data.note: Robbie Colgan partners this Donal Kinsella-trained 3-year-old carrying a fade flag and two runs both finishing 12th and 13th on Good ground; 38 days since last run and no encouraging form signal makes this one of the harder cases to construct a positive argument for.|

runners_data.name: Churchfield Lady
runners_data.note: Shane Foley — a high-class booking for Mrs John Harrington — partners this filly whose two runs came on Soft, meaning today's Good ground is an unresolved question; she is a natural hold-up horse whose best position is the rear, now squeezed into a midfield role, and the jockey quality is the strongest thing in her corner.|

runners_data.name: Contrite
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a standout booking for D K Weld (T14: 3/13), and 78 days off the track with a hood (hg:t) suggests this return has been planned; the form shows a fair 4th on Soft at 8f but today's Good ground and 1m1½f trip are both unknowns — a well-supported latecomer whose true closing style is compromised by the crowded rear of this field.|

runners_data.name: Guinelot
runners_data.note: K J Condon fields a second runner in Guinelot (headgear: h), lightly raced over 12f on Good and 10f on Soft for just two runs; the unknown style flag and unexposed profile make this one of the more open questions, and the step back to 1m1½f from a 12f debut effort on Good is worth monitoring as a potential trip-softener.|

races.paceDynamic: Taj Crown is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner maiden and, with no other genuine pace horse to challenge for the lead, W J Lee should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over the 1m1½f trip at Ballinrobe on Good ground. The field behind Taj Crown is dominated by natural hold-up horses — Half Cut, Tyraxes, Countertop, Churchfield Lady and Contrite are all true closers who have been mapped to midfield purely because there is nowhere else to place them, meaning the rear of the field will be crowded and tactical options compressed. Avec Grand Plaisir and Guinelot carry unknown or unresolved style profiles and could add minor positional interest, but neither is likely to seriously contest the lead with Taj Crown. This uncontested pace sets up a race that strongly favours horses who can travel close to or just behind the leader in the prominent-to-midfield bracket, as the genuine hold-up horses will be trapped in a slowly-strung-out convoy with little daylight to weave through late; the tactical verdict is clear — positional horses who can latch onto Taj Crown's measured gallop are best placed, with true closers fighting against their own field positioning.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Taj Crown Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Taj Crown is allowed to stride to the front unchallenged and sets a steady, controlled pace that suits a prominent hold-up-in-touch runner.
scenarios.body: Taj Crown dictates from the front on a fair but unhurried tempo, and the horses who travel just behind in second and third have the clearest passage into the straight; on Good ground at this trip, a strong finishing horse sitting second or third off a sustainable pace is ideally placed to overhaul a front-runner who has conserved energy.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Produces Muddling Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled that it creates a bunched, slow-motion race where several horses finish in a heap in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early tempo causes maximum traffic problems for the hold-up horses trapped in the middle of the pack, while Taj Crown and any horse travelling prominently still has a clear advantage at the top of the straight; the winner is likely to be the horse with the freshest legs and clearest run, rewarding those who managed to find a prominent berth early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just quick enough to string the field out and one of the repositioned closers manages to find a gap and rattle home late.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped to midfield out of natural role, a horse like Contrite (D K Weld, Colin Keane) or Churchfield Lady (Shane Foley, Mrs Harrington) could find daylight if the field spreads wide in the straight; this scenario requires an improbable sequence of gap-finding given how many closers are bunched together, making it the least-reliable outcome for that profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unknown Unexposed Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced or unknown-style runners like Guinelot or Noble Venture turns out to be significantly better than their form suggests and outpaces the field in the straight.
scenarios.body: Guinelot, wearing headgear and lightly raced over Good ground at 12f, could improve markedly on debut form if the trip and conditions unlock improvement; Noble Venture, also lightly exposed over this sort of trip, represents the wildcard for a yard that sends runners to Ballinrobe selectively.

watchPoints.text: Taj Crown (W J Lee / K J Condon) faces no pace rival whatsoever — watch whether he gets completely unchallenged to the lead from the gate, because if he does, the race is run entirely on his terms and all other scenarios collapse into this one shape.

Contrite (Colin Keane / D K Weld) is 78 days off the track, wearing a hood for the first time, and arrives with a serious jockey-trainer combination — watch the market for a move that would suggest stable confidence on this return from a break.

Churchfield Lady (Shane Foley / Mrs Harrington) has run exclusively on Soft ground; watch the going report at declaration time and track conditions underfoot — any overnight drying that firms the surface makes her form entirely unexposed at this level.

Shay's Dream carries the Dylan Browne McMonagle booking for Joseph O'Brien despite three zero-form runs — watch whether that jockey-trainer combination is significant or simply a retained retainer fill-in, as the difference in confidence level is substantial.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Half Cut, Tyraxes, Countertop, Churchfield Lady, Contrite) will all be jostling for midfield positions they do not naturally want — watch the first two furlongs for congestion and any horse that emerges naturally into a prominent position without being pushed there, as that runner has found a tactical edge the pace map does not show.

runners_data.name: Werifesteria
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Mrs Harrington and Shane Foley; three recent runs all on good ground over 12f show consistent pace-setting but modest finishing positions (7-8-7), suggesting she leads but stops, making her vulnerable if Mare Crisium pushes her harder than usual from the gun.
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of her last three starts (7th, 8th, 7th) and without a win in that time. She has run over today's going before, but a yard managing just 0/27 in the last fortnight and a rating that ranks her only 11th of 13 leave her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a fading-in-finish flag; form reads 9-11-10 at shorter distances, and this step up to 1m1½f on good ground is a new ask — Rory Cleary's booking is the main positive but this horse has not shown the ability to sustain late effort.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in his last two starts and a ninth three starts back, he remains without a win in that spell. He has run over today's going before, and ranked 7th of 13 on our figures, he looks more of a make-up-the-numbers type than a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose form string includes a win at 8f on standard ground and three placed efforts, making him one of the more solid form-horses in the field; Donagh O'Connor rides, and at 1m1½f on good ground the trip looks a workable step up with hood reported in headgear.
runners_data.comment: Below-par when seventh last time out, but that followed a win two starts back and a pair of fourths before it — a genuinely progressive profile. He has run over today's distance and going before, and that combination makes him our confident pick.

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for De Bromhead, which commands attention, but Divine Believer has faded in finish across all recent outings and has only one run on good ground from five recent starts; a 71-day absence and consistently poor finishing positions make this a difficult trust at this trip.
runners_data.comment: A rating that ranks her 4th of 13 gives her claims among the leading dangers, and she has run over today's going before. But her recent form is modest — 8th, 7th and 7th, with two unplaced efforts before that — leaving her without a win after a 71-day break.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, ridden by apprentice Max Popan (10lb claim) for K J Condon; has raced over 10-12f without threatening the frame on soft and heavy — the switch to a firmer surface and this clear front-running role may suit better, but the apprentice claim in a pace battle is a risk factor.
runners_data.comment: Modest recent form reads 9th, 5th, 8th and 6th, leaving her without a win in that spell, though a fifth two starts back shows she can be competitive. She is out again quickly, just 12 days since her last run, but a rating that ranks her only 9th of 13 caps her claims.

runners_data.name: Private Larry
runners_data.note: Ran just three days ago over 17f on good ground and finished third, demonstrating both freshness and versatility; his most recent win came over 12f on good ground for Alan McIntyre, and the ability to race handily from a hold-up base suits the expected race shape well with Gavin Ryan aboard.
runners_data.comment: He won last time out, bouncing back from a spell of modest efforts (8th, 8th and three unplaced runs before that), and he's quick to follow up just three days later. He has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating that ranks him 5th of 13 makes him respected in this company.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in nature — placed at 7f on heavy and twice on softer ground — reassigned to midfield on the map because of overcrowding at the rear; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects that racing mid-division rather than from off the pace is not ideal for Siobhan Rutledge's mount.
runners_data.comment: Rated 3rd of 13, she's among the leading dangers, with a runner-up effort two starts back showing she has the class to figure. She has run over today's distance before, but remains without a win in that spell, and her trainer is just 0/28 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Spring Sprinter
runners_data.note: Ben Coen is a strong booking for Andrew Slattery, but this horse has finished 12th, 6th, and 7th in three career starts, all on good ground over 8-10f — a true hold-up type nudged onto the map into midfield given the depth of closers in this field, and the STYLE_FIT discount (0.90) reflects the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out and beaten into 6th and 7th before that, she remains without a win in her last three starts. She has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating that ranks her 8th of 13 puts her firmly in the pack rather than among the leading players.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Terry Casey (7lb) rides for Michael Mulvany; a true hold-up type whose best recent effort was 4th over 9f on good ground, though also 5th over 13f most recently — mapped to midfield due to overcrowding, and at OR 51 this is a lower-rated runner whose chance is most realistic only if the race falls apart for others.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, with two fourth finishes among his last six starts, he remains without a win in that run, though he is quick back into action just three days later. He has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating that ranks him 6th of 13 keeps him firmly involved.

runners_data.name: Curious Jane
runners_data.note: A natural closer carrying a fades-in-finish flag and redistributed to midfield on the map; form of 0-0-0-9 does not inspire confidence at this level, and the combination of positional compromise and habitual fading makes this a difficult proposition for Nathan Crosse despite the return from 32 days off.
runners_data.comment: A ninth and three further unplaced efforts make up her recent form, leaving her without a win in that spell. She has run over today's distance before, but a rating that ranks her only 12th of 13 leaves her hard to fancy from this field.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides for Sheila Lavery; the form line includes 3rd and 4th at 10f on good ground, and at OR 45 this is arguably the most form-consistent of the lower-rated redistributed closers — bumped to midfield on the map but the placed efforts on matching conditions keep this horse in the conversation for place money.
runners_data.comment: Top of our ratings, she was third last time out, and fourth two starts back, useful recent form despite being without a win in that time. She has run over today's distance and going before, and looks the biggest threat in this field on pure figures.

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce (3lb) on a horse that has finished between 6th and 10th in six consecutive starts on good ground for Paul Flynn; the fades-in-finish tag compounds a STYLE_FIT of 0.92, and with six runs without a win or placing on identical going, the evidence argues strongly against this one.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of her last six starts — 9th, unplaced, 7th, 6th, 9th and unplaced — and still without a win in that run. She has run over today's going before, but ranked bottom of the field on our figures, she's hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan (5lb) rides for Thomas Dowling; five recent starts at 10f on good and soft ground show a fading-in-finish pattern and no wins, and this horse is a natural hold-up type reassigned to midfield — the combination of apprentice rider, low OR (40), and flagged finishing weakness leaves it with very little margin for error.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record of 5th, 4th, unplaced, 6th, 9th and 9th leaves her without a win in her last six starts. She has run over today's distance and going before, but a rating that ranks her only 10th of 13 makes her hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Werifesteria and Mare Crisium are the two confirmed front-runners in a 13-runner field, and with both likely to press for the early lead, this race will be run at an honest, contested gallop from the outset over 1m1½f on good ground at Ballinrobe. Werifesteria (Shane Foley, Mrs John Harrington) has shown consistent front-running tendencies across recent good-ground starts, while Mare Crisium (Max Popan) will also seek to get across and dictate, meaning neither will get a soft lead. The resulting pace scenario — two horses fighting for the front — sets up a race where the early energy is burned by the leaders, creating conditions that should favour horses able to travel prominently just off the pace or those with a genuine late kick from midfield. However, the field contains far more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Aquilla Star, Spring Sprinter, Nephin Mountain, Curious Jane, Connova, Six Wings, and Music And Song are all redistributed from their natural hold-up positions into midfield slots — meaning horses capable of racing prominently just off the two leaders, such as Private Larry and John La Bear, are best placed to capitalise if the front-runners tie each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Chasers
scenarios.trigger: If Werifesteria and Mare Crisium push each other through a genuine early gallop, draining both before the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other's reserves in the first half of the race, handing advantage to horses who travel just off the pace with cover and produce a strong sustained finish; Private Larry's recent good-ground form and ability to sit handy is directly relevant here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium or Werifesteria secures a clear, uncontested lead and the other settles into a prominent position without a prolonged duel.
scenarios.body: One front-runner dictates a controlled pace, conserves energy through the middle, and kicks clear in the straight before the hold-up types can close; Werifesteria's good-ground record and the Harrington/Foley combination give this a credible chance of materialising.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or proves uneven enough for the midfield-mapped horses to arrive late in a bunched finish.
scenarios.body: Several redistributed hold-up horses — Aquilla Star, Spring Sprinter, Connova — would need to race genuinely out of their natural role to deliver this outcome, which the STYLE_FIT tags rightly discount; Connova's placed efforts on good ground at 10f represent the most credible version of this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace fractures the field dramatically, causing interference or multiple horses to drop away, resulting in a messy, strung-out finish.
scenarios.body: An unruly early duel involving Werifesteria and Mare Crisium in a large, moderate-class field can create uneven sectionals that randomise the outcome; Divine Believer and Coolshine, both flagged as finishers who fade, are unlikely beneficiaries but hold long-shot claims if the race falls apart unusually.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Werifesteria or Mare Crisium blinks first at the start — if both fly out together and engage in a prolonged duel through the opening half-mile, the leader scenario collapses in value and horses tracking them like Private Larry and John La Bear become the primary beneficiaries.

Private Larry ran just three days ago and the quick turnaround for Gavin Ryan's mount is worth monitoring in the parade ring — if the horse shows any signs of residual fatigue from the 17f effort, its ability to travel prominently and sustain the run home is compromised.

Mare Crisium is ridden by apprentice Max Popan (10lb claim) in a direct pace battle — if the inexperience of the claimer sees the horse either sent too fast too soon or restrained and unable to assert, the race shape pivots sharply and the front-runner scenario loses its second pillar.

Connova and Nephin Mountain are the most credible of the redistributed hold-up types based on form consistency at this trip and going — if the early pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders, watch both to emerge from midfield in the closing stages as potential each-way claims at bigger prices.

The sheer number of hold-up horses in this field (seven redistributed) means the closing stages could see a congested bunch of horses arriving together — any horse able to find a clear passage from a handy mid-race position, such as John La Bear with hood, holds a tactical edge over those stuck wide or blocked.

races.name: Daily Sports Special At Tote.ie Handicap

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer dropping back from longer trips, Jack Cleary (5) takes the mount for Grassick whose yard is 1/4 in the 14-day window; last ran 12 days ago and has fair similar-going form (9/15) but the 1m1½f trip looks on the short side for a horse who needs races to develop strongly.|
runners_data.comment: Loingseoir's recent form reads modestly — no better than fourth in his last five starts and winless throughout — but a rating well clear of his 69 official mark suggests more is possible. He has run over today's trip and going before and heads this field on figures.

runners_data.name: Bucaneer's Spirit
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race and likely to dictate from the off on Good ground that suits (12/15 sim-going strike rate); trained by Donoghue whose yard is 0/9 in the 14-day window, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 reflects that this horse is recorded as a prominent racer who may be operating slightly out of role as a pure leader — temper expectations accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Bucaneer's Spirit was a close second last time out, having also finished third on two occasions in this sequence, though he remains winless. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 72 puts him firmly amongst the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Lady Chartwell
runners_data.note: A consistent tail-ender whose form figures (500-00) tell a stark story on Good and Standard ground; Luke McAteer takes over for Sweeney and the horse has been well beaten in all five recent starts including three at this trip and beyond — hard to see a route to the frame.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Chartwell's finishing positions have been modest — no better than fifth in five starts and winless throughout — but a rating well clear of her 65 official mark suggests she is capable of more. She has run over today's trip and going before, and that gap keeps her among the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: Colin Keane picks up the ride for Molloy, and this four-year-old has solid Good-ground form (13/15 sim-going) with a recent placed run at 10f and 11f suggesting the 1m1½f trip at Ballinrobe is right in the zone; a genuine prominent racer whose natural position just off the lead is ideal for this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Elusive Duke has been runner-up twice and third once in his last five starts, without adding a win. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a strong speed figure gives him claims, though a rating of 66 keeps him more midfield than leading contender.

runners_data.name: Metamorphic
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount for Harrington, but the form figures (359-96) over 10f-13f on Good-to-Soft and Standard ground are modest; the yard is 0/27 in 14 days suggesting a stable out of form, and Metamorphic has shown no ability to win on Good ground in recent starts.|
runners_data.comment: Metamorphic's form has faded since finishing third five starts back, dipping to two ninths before a modest sixth last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 68 is tempered by a cold yard, without a winner from 27 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse with worrying form (000-00 in most recent runs) who wears blinkers; Adrian McGuinness is 2/28 in the 14-day window and the horse has finished in the bottom half of every field it has contested in recent starts — hard to find encouragement regardless of race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Dancing Steve has failed to finish in the frame in any of his last five starts and remains without a win. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a notably strong speed figure hints at ability not yet showing up in the results.

runners_data.name: Lady Arwen
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft last time but is a true hold-up racer being pushed closer to the pace than she'd prefer by the density of hold-up horses in this field; W J Lee takes the ride for O'Dwyer, returns after 38 days off, and her best form has come over shorter on softer ground — both factors work against her here.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Arwen won three starts back but has failed to build on that since, following up with sixth and an unplaced effort last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and on a rating of 62 she remains one of the outsiders here.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides for Fahey, and this mare has a tidy placed record over 10f-13f on Good ground, including a recent third at 12f; she's a genuine hold-up performer who needs a truly run race to deliver her best and the moderate projected tempo in this field is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Miss Crinshawn has been admirably consistent, never finishing worse than fourth in her last five starts, but a win has proved elusive throughout. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 63 reflects a solid if unspectacular formline that keeps her in the mix.

runners_data.name: Signor Ferrari
runners_data.note: A long absence of 419 days is the major red flag here — last ran in May 2024 and returns for Murphy whose yard is 0/3 in the 14-day window; has won over 10f on Standard going and showed promise at Naas before the layoff, but ring rust after well over a year off must be a significant discount.|
runners_data.comment: Signor Ferrari won five starts back and signed off that sequence with a third last time out, form that stands up despite a lengthy 419-day absence since. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 68 makes him a leading danger if fitness allows.

runners_data.name: Brewel Hill
runners_data.note: The 10-year-old veteran for McCreery has a solid Good-ground profile (12/15 sim-going) and placed at 10f and 12f in recent starts, but is a true hold-up type who won't get the natural position at the rear this field demands; the STYLE_FIT flag and redistribution note both caution against assuming it can operate as a late finisher.|
runners_data.comment: Brewel Hill has been up and down in his last five starts, sandwiching a third between two unplaced efforts, and remains without a win. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 65 keeps him competitive without standing out among the leading names.

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's yard is hot (3/21 in 14 days) and this six-year-old arrives in strong form — won his last race over 9f Good and has a 2W3P record in similar going; a genuine prominent racer who handles Good ground well, and Leigh Roche has the experience to place him correctly just off the leader.|
runners_data.comment: Nibras Rainbow won last time out and was also successful four starts back, sandwiching a runner-up and a third in between — a string of solid placings in this sequence. He has run over today's trip and going before, but a modest rating of 58 leaves him among the outsiders.

runners_data.name: Real Petite
runners_data.note: Winner over 8f Good earlier in the campaign but has struggled at 13f and 16f since, and the ⚠ fade flag is relevant — finishes weakly when the race develops; Jimmy Dalton (7) is an inexperienced claimer and, as a true hold-up type operating out of role in a field with too many hold-up horses, the map position is a concession to field shape rather than a reflection of natural running style.|
runners_data.comment: Real Petite won three starts back but has since faded, following up with sixth and an unplaced effort last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 51 places her firmly among the outsiders in this field.

runners_data.name: Cuckaloo Hill
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride for Flannery on a filly whose recent form (04005) is poor, and the ⚠ fade flag echoes a tendency to weaken in the closing stages; as another genuine hold-up type compressed into midfield by the field configuration, she arrives off a 28-day break without the race shape likely to bring out her best.|
runners_data.comment: Cuckaloo Hill has managed no better than fourth in her last five starts, with three unplaced efforts in that sequence, and remains without a win. She has run over today's trip and going before, but a rating of 47 — the field's lowest — leaves her with a mountain to climb.

races.paceDynamic: Bucaneer's Spirit is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap over 1m1½f at Ballinrobe, and with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge for the lead, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured. The prominent types — Elusive Duke, Dancing Steve, Nibras Rainbow, and Signor Ferrari — will likely settle just behind her, meaning the pace is unlikely to be falsely strong, favouring those who can race handily and produce a sustained run rather than a late burst. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses: Lady Arwen, Brewel Hill, Real Petite, and Cuckaloo Hill are all true hold-up types who cannot get their natural rear position in this field configuration and will be forced closer to the pace than suits them, reducing their effectiveness as genuine late finishers. This race shape — a single uncontested leader, a moderate gallop, and a cluster of prominent-to-midfield runners — strongly favours those who can race in the first four or five with cover and quicken off a turning tempo: prominent or handy-midfield types who handle Good ground and stay the trip are the clear beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bucaneer Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Bucaneer's Spirit leads uncontested and sets a fair-to-moderate pace that suits prominent racers off her back.
scenarios.body: Bucaneer's Spirit controls affairs from flag to finish on Good ground at a track she handles, and the runners best placed to challenge are those tracking her closely in the first three or four positions; with no pace duel to exploit, hold-up horses find too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Elusive Duke or Nibras Rainbow press forward early and race in the slipstream of the leader throughout, delivering their challenge turning for home.
scenarios.body: The tempo stays controlled but honest enough that horses who race handy through the race are rewarded over those required to come from off the pace; with Colin Keane aboard Elusive Duke and Nibras Rainbow in red-hot recent form, either can challenge the front-runner decisively.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than expected and front-runners tie each other up, allowing a genuine staying-type from midfield to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Miss Crinshawn or Loingseoir, both true hold-up types suited to longer distances and Good ground, could benefit from a strung-out finish if the tempo quickens unusually early; however, with the pace map showing a moderate single leader, this is a secondary rather than primary shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a strong enough gallop to set up a genuine late run from the back of the field.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses tagged as redistributed — Lady Arwen, Brewel Hill, Real Petite, and Cuckaloo Hill — racing at the rear as true hold-up types, but the field configuration means they are unlikely to get that position naturally; the scenario is significantly discounted because the horses who would deliver it are not operating in their true role.

watchPoints.text: Bucaneer's Spirit has the lead to herself but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) signals she is recorded as a prominent rather than true front-runner — watch whether Sam Coen allows her to stride clear or if she is uncomfortable dictating, as any hesitation at the front opens the race up immediately.

Nibras Rainbow and Elusive Duke are both genuine prominent types with strong recent form and high-calibre jockeys (Leigh Roche and Colin Keane respectively) — if either pushes to dispute the lead early, even a moderate pace duel could transform the race shape and bring closers into play.

Signor Ferrari returns after 419 days absent with no public trial work visible; watch his early market moves and paddock demeanour closely — any sign of freshness or being light in condition would make him very hard to trust regardless of his pre-absence form.

Lady Arwen, Brewel Hill, Real Petite, and Cuckaloo Hill are all true hold-up horses who cannot all settle at the rear as preferred — whichever is widest or meets traffic at the back is most disadvantaged; watch the opening quarter-mile for runners being shuffled further back than their jockeys want.|

Miss Crinshawn has consistent placed form over longer trips and Ben Coen is a strong partner, but she needs a strong gallop to close from midfield — if the tempo is as modest as the single-leader map suggests, watch whether Coen elects to ride her closer to the pace than usual to compensate.|

races.name: Tote.ie Everyday Is A Money Back Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Londonofficecallin
runners_data.note: Course and distance form is strong (9 runs at similar trips and going, three wins, five places), Gavin Cromwell stable has decent 14-day strike rate, and a prominent style maps naturally onto this race shape; 20 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and was also successful four starts back, with a ninth and an unplaced effort sandwiched between those victories. He has run over today's distance and going before, and that solid recent form plus a fitness edge make him a confident selection despite not topping our figures.

runners_data.name: Truth Be Told
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; won his last two at 10f and 12f on Good, but steps up to 1m5f for the first time and has been off 71 days — stamina and fitness are the questions if the gallop is tested late.
runners_data.comment: Won his last two starts, following a fourth, a ninth and a fifth before that, form that puts him right among the leading dangers. He has run over today's distance and going before, but he is back after a lengthy 71-day absence, which is the main question mark.

runners_data.name: War Rooms
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has struggled for form recently (four runs without a place finish in current sequence), Colin Keane takes the ride, but going and trip aren't a concern — the issue is whether the pace is honest enough to bring him into play; previous headgear (p) not worn here.
runners_data.comment: Top of our ratings for this race, his figures of unplaced, 8th, unplaced, 7th and 6th look modest, but those runs have come in better company. He has run over today's distance and going before, though he remains without a win in that spell and returns from a 58-day break.

runners_data.name: Royal Saxo
runners_data.note: All three career wins came on Standard (AW) going, and similar-going turf record reads just 1 from 12 — the Good turf surface is a genuine query despite decent recent form; prominent style suits the likely race shape.
runners_data.comment: Well held in his last two starts (9th, 9th), though that followed a stronger run — second three starts back, a winner four starts back, and second five starts back. Ranked only 9th of 10 on our figures, he's hard to fancy without more of that earlier form to call upon.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 12f and 13f on Good suggest the trip and ground are fine, and the trainer has a 1-from-1 recent strike; however, with several prominent types in the field, this horse's natural tracking position may be squeezed out, which blunts the effectiveness that produced those wins.
runners_data.comment: Won her last two starts, an improved spell after a pair of fifths in the two runs before that and an unplaced run further back. She has run over today's distance and going before, but a rating that ranks her only 8th of 10 makes her one to note rather than fancy strongly here.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Ran just nine days ago and the blinkers are on again; a prominent racer at a short enough trip historically, so stepping to 1m5f is a question, but recent form shows he handles the grade and Gary Carroll is a positive booking.
runners_data.comment: Modest form of late — fourth last time out and largely held in this spell, though a second three starts back hints at more when things click. He has run over today's distance and going before, but he remains without a win, and a rating that ranks him only 7th of 10 leaves him hard to fancy strongly.

runners_data.name: Sea Coral
runners_data.note: The form string of 20-003 masks a placed effort at 12f on Good going — the trip is well within range and trainer Mrs John Harrington's hold-up types can improve sharply on quicker going; needs a stronger gallop than this race may produce to hit the line.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and second five starts back, either side of three unplaced efforts, still without a win in that run. She has run over today's distance and going before, and a rating that ranks her 5th of 10 keeps her in the mix, despite her yard's runners managing just 0/27 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Leggagh
runners_data.note: A long absence of 273 days is an immediate concern, and while this horse has won at 12f on Soft, its true prominent style will be difficult to express in a field stacked with front-trackers; the Rafferty 10lb claim helps offset the weight, but fitness is the primary doubt.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, and fifth two starts back, though a win three starts back shows the quality he can produce on his day. He has run over today's distance and going before, but a lengthy 273-day absence is the obvious concern, and a rating ranks him only 6th of 10.

runners_data.name: Deralo Ir
runners_data.note: Off 407 days — by far the longest absence in the field — and only two career runs to draw on; a natural prominent runner who will find this packed pace map unhelpful on return from over a year off, and the AJ Martin yard has a modest recent strike rate.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, though a second two starts back and another second four starts back show he has been competitive in this grade. He is unexposed and returns after 407 days off, leaving plenty of scope for more than his recent finishes suggest.

runners_data.name: Pillar Of Hope
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has raced prominently throughout a long career, but recent form shows nothing better than fourth and the Patrick McGettigan 5lb claim can only do so much; the enforced midfield berth in this field genuinely works against what this horse does naturally.
runners_data.comment: A rating that ranks him 4th of 10 puts him among the leading dangers, and a fourth last time out shows he's holding his form. He has run over today's distance and going before, but he remains without a win in that spell and returns from a 46-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Truth Be Told is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with a clear lead expected, should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this flat 1m5f trip on Good ground. The real complication is the density of prominent-style horses behind — Daboya, Duke Of Leggagh, Deralo Ir, and Pillar Of Hope are all natural trackers who cannot all occupy the positions they want, meaning at least several will be forced to race further back than ideal. Londonofficecallin and Royal Saxo are genuine prominent types who may be better placed to actually secure that ground immediately behind the leader, while the redistributed horses will be racing at least partially out of role. The race shape strongly favours a confirmed prominent racer who can settle just off Truth Be Told's controlled gallop and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a true hold-up horse who needs a strong pace to chase down will find this tempo insufficient.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Truth Be Told Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Truth Be Told leads from the front without serious early pressure and controls tempo throughout the 1m5f.
scenarios.body: Truth Be Told sets a comfortable, measured pace on Good ground and, with no horse willing or able to take it on early, reaches the straight with energy in reserve; a prominent racer who has tracked closely and transitioned smoothly is best placed to chase and challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Sweeps Past
scenarios.trigger: If Truth Be Told's lead is accepted but a close-tracking prominent type times their move perfectly in the straight.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace means those who have settled just off the leader are full of running turning in, allowing the best of them to overhaul Truth Be Told in the final furlong; this suits a horse who has genuine Good-ground form at the trip and a confident jockey hold.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Comes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front two burn each other out, leaving room for a hold-up type to finish past them.
scenarios.body: War Coral or Sea Coral, racing patiently towards the rear, benefit if the tempo picks up sufficiently to string the field out and create a genuinely-run race over this staying trip; this scenario is conditional on the pace being more honest than Truth Be Told's profile suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments early and a displaced prominent horse — Daboya, Duke Of Leggagh, or Pillar Of Hope — finds an unexpectedly clear passage from their enforced midfield berth.
scenarios.body: Racing out of their natural role reduces their effectiveness, but a messy, strung-out race could allow one of these horses to produce a sustained run if others tire; the low probability reflects how much they are compromised by the field's pace density.

watchPoints.text: Truth Be Told has been off 71 days and steps up sharply in trip to 1m5f — monitor how he moves in the paddock and whether W J Lee opts to conserve energy early or press on, as fitness and stamina doubts could unwind the entire pace map if he stops.

Daboya, Duke Of Leggagh, Pillar Of Hope, and Deralo Ir are all natural prominent racers who cannot all get their position — watch the first two furlongs for crowding and shuffling back, which could cause interference and disrupt the running order materially.

Duke Of Leggagh returns from 273 days off and Deralo Ir from 407 days — both are prominent types who will be pushed wide or back in a packed pace map; if either shows distress early or is pulled up, the midfield becomes extremely congested.

Royal Saxo's form was built almost entirely on AW Standard going — three wins from three on that surface — and today's Good turf is a different test; if the ground is riding quicker than expected, watch how he travels in the early stages as a guide to whether he handles it.

Sea Coral is the most interesting hold-up horse if the pace quickens — Shane Foley booked for a horse who finished third at 12f on Good last time, and any sign of Truth Be Told increasing the tempo mid-race would bring this runner into the late-race conversation.

races.name: Racing, Sports & Games At Tote.ie Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Tassarolo

runners_data.comment: Tassarolo has been busy without a win in his last six starts, the form reading 3rd, 8th, 5th, 5th, 3rd and 9th. Race-fit just five days after his latest outing, he has experience over today's trip and ground, and is rated 58 with us.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: True hold-up type dropping back from distances up to 20f, with apprentice Adam Browne-Souza claiming 7lb; trainer Andrew Slattery is active (3/32 in 14 days) and the horse's best form has come around 10-12f, so the stamina test at 1m5f on Good ground is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Preparations boasts a smart speed figure of 77 and experience over today's trip and ground, rating second of eleven at 65. She was unplaced when last seen ten days ago, though, and remains without a win in her last five starts despite a fourth three starts back.

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran with a single win from 15 similar-going starts but with a course-and-distance type profile on Good turf; fitted with tongue-tie, Conor Cusack claims 7lb, and a 18-day absence after a run that included a win over 14f on Soft suggests connections are targeting this trip deliberately.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, Desert Friend can point to a win four starts back, sandwiched by finishes of ninth, ninth and third. He has run over today's trip and ground before and returns fit despite 18 days off, rated 56 with us.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose recent form figures read 000590, suggesting sporadic ability; fitted with tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and a 38-day break is notable — Jimmy Dalton claims 7lb and the horse's sim-going record (8/15, one win, four places) points to competence on Good ground if the headgear sparks a revival.
runners_data.comment: Giselles Defence has struggled for form, without a win in his last six starts and only a ninth and a fifth to show among four unplaced efforts. He has experience over today's trip and ground, but a 38-day break and a 56 rating leave him needing more.

runners_data.name: Kings Gesture
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose form shows a recurring tendency to fade in the finish, with zero wins or places from six similar-going starts; 129-day absence is a significant concern, and though Sam Coen claims 2lb, the horse is shown in midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed — its natural instinct to race last will be hard to express.
runners_data.comment: Kings Gesture has raced over today's trip before and rates a strong fourth of eleven at 59, well above his official mark of 52. The concern is fitness, though, after 129 days off and a five-start sequence without a win that included an eighth and two fifths.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Prominent type who should push forward behind Tassarolo and represents one of the few horses likely to get a natural position in this race shape; Jack Cleary rides and the horse has placed twice from four recent runs, including a second over 10f on Soft — the step up to 1m5f on Good ground is the key stamina query.
runners_data.comment: Trishuli River has experience over today's trip and ground and rates third of eleven at 63, well clear of her official mark of 52. She has been unplaced in her last two starts, though, leaving her winless in that run despite a second and a third earlier in the sequence.

runners_data.name: Autocrat
runners_data.note: Recurring finisher who tends to fade, with zero wins from four similar-going efforts and a headgear note of blinkers; despite being a genuine hold-up type, the overcrowded rear of the field means Mel Sheridan (7lb claim) will likely find this one racing closer than ideal — the horse's OR 48 reflects a modest level and recent form of 417000 is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Autocrat won five starts back and has experience over today's trip and ground, rating the form pick here at 71, the highest of the eleven runners. He returns fit nine days on from a quieter run, but on these figures he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a striking recent form string of 55132, including a win and two places at 12-13f on Good; Rory Mulligan claims 2lb for John McConnell and the horse ran just three days ago, which is a stamina-and-freshness flag, but the good-ground form and upward trajectory make this one of the more interesting profiles in the race despite its redistribution from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Masego won three starts back and was runner-up last time out, and he has experience over today's trip and ground. But the trainer is 0 from 28 in the last fortnight, and he rates bottom of the field at 43 despite a useful speed figure of 65.

runners_data.name: Reflectionist
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose last five runs are littered with double-figure finishes at distances up to 20f on Good ground — sim-going record of 10/15 masks two wins but recent figures (9-10-10-?-11) suggest a horse running below its best; Joseph Harnett claims 7lb but the age and deteriorating form make it hard to construct a winning scenario even in a moderate field.
runners_data.comment: Reflectionist has struggled for form, without a win in his last five starts and no better than eighth among three further unplaced efforts. He has experience over today's trip and ground, returns fit thirteen days on, and is rated 54 with us.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a record that includes two seconds at 10-12f, wearing blinkers and carrying OR 45; Jack Kearney rides for A Oliver (2/22 in 14 days, an active yard), and while the horse's natural hold-up instinct pushes it toward the rear, the shorter trip profile in its history (all runs at 10-12f) raises a genuine 1m5f stamina question.
runners_data.comment: Copper Craft was runner-up last time out and has two more places to his name in his last five starts, without a win in that time. He has experience over today's trip and ground, fit nine days on, and rates near the bottom of the field at 48.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying just 119lbs with a 2lb claim from Patrick McGettigan, but all five career runs have been at 7-11f and on Good or Standard ground — the step to 1m5f is a significant, unproven stamina test; Patrick Magee's yard is in decent form (4/11 in 14 days) but the horse fades in finishes and its redistribution to midfield masks a true hold-up nature.
runners_data.comment: Wingit's recent form reads 5th, 9th, 6th, unplaced and 6th, leaving her without a win in that spell. She has experience of today's going and returns quickly six days on, but sits towards the foot of our ratings at 49.

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected from the field, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m5f trip on Good ground at Ballinrobe. Trishuli River is the only other likely early mover, and while Kings Gesture, Autocrat, Wingit, and Masego all carry prominent or hold-up tendencies, the field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types who will be forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style demands. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Tassarolo and Trishuli River are most likely to actually secure the prominent positions, with the rest shuffled into a compressed midfield. This race shape strongly favours hold-up or midfield runners who can travel smoothly behind a lone, uncontested leader and produce a sustained late run, as the controlled early fractions will not expose the front-runner until the home straight, rewarding those with the stamina and finishing kick to reel in a fresh front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tassarolo Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo leads from the front without pressure and sets a moderate, energy-conserving pace that suits a strong finishing run.
scenarios.body: Tassarolo dictates throughout on a comfortable tempo, leaving the hold-up brigade with plenty of horse turning for home but needing to find plenty of ground in a short straight; horses who travel fluently in midfield and produce a sustained rather than sharp finish will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field, allowing several midfield types to deliver a wall of finishing runs simultaneously in the straight.
scenarios.body: The uniform gallop means the gap between front and rear is minimal at the home turn, and runners who have settled just off the pace — rather than deep hold-up — will have the positional advantage to pounce; those with recent good-ground form and stamina for the 1m5f trip will thrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that Tassarolo's energy reserves are largely intact entering the straight, making the front-runner impossible to catch.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian gallop means the hold-up horses burn more energy closing than Tassarolo spends leading, and the leader's fresh legs carry it clear before the closers can organise; Trishuli River, prominent throughout, would be best placed of the chasers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If a mid-race injection of pace from a prominent runner scrambles the field order and causes the race to fracture unpredictably in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: An unexpected surge in tempo forces hold-up runners to commit earlier than ideal and exposes those out of their natural position; horses with a proven ability to handle messy tactical races and with genuine finishing stamina over this sort of trip will benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Tassarolo's energy reserves are the hinge of this race — watch how strongly it travels at the head of affairs in the first mile, because a fresh front-runner who gets an uncontested lead at a reasonable pace over 1m5f on Good ground can prove extremely hard to reel in with a short Ballinrobe straight.

Masego ran just three days ago and that turnaround is unusually quick — watch for signs of fatigue in the final furlong, as its recent form is the best in the race but a bounce effect at this trip could undermine what looks a promising profile.

Kings Gesture (129-day absence) and Wingit (unproven beyond 11f) both carry significant absence or stamina risks — if either fails to stay the 1m5f trip, they could create positional disruption as they back out of the bridle in the closing stages and force other runners to switch.

With six of the eleven runners showing a tendency to fade in the finish or tagged with redistribution away from their natural hold-up role, watch the home turn for a compressed, scrimmaging group — runners who have managed to find a clear passage on the outside entering the straight will have a decisive positional edge.

Patrick Magee's yard is 4/11 in the last 14 days, making Wingit worth monitoring in the market despite the inexperience at this trip — a significant market move would suggest connections have reason to believe the stamina question is answered.

races.name: Follow Tote On X Maiden

runners_data.name: Black Heather
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer with solid Good-ground credentials (9 from 13 sim-going runs, two wins), Dylan Browne McMonagle-trained stablemate not aboard here — Whearty takes the ride — and the 1m5f trip sits within a proven range; the key angle is whether the pace is honest enough to allow a sustained late run, which Pampar Lady's controlled style only partially guarantees.

runners_data.name: Catalani
runners_data.note: Jack Foley's seven-year-old boasts a striking win over 23f last time and confirmed Good-ground form (5 from 6), but his natural front-to-prominent style has been pushed back into a mapped midfield position in this shape — Ben Coen will face a tactical puzzle managing a horse that wants to bowl along rather than be restrained.

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins sends this five-year-old out with a 1m trip win already on Good ground and a 52-day break, but the fade-in-finish flag is the defining concern here — over 1m5f against rivals who stay better, getting outpointed late is a real risk, and his two Soft-ground efforts were poor.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: An apprentice-ridden prominent runner with a 1m1f Good-ground win and three placings from five sim-going runs; a 17-day turnaround is fine, and Robyn Donaghue-Leahy's 7lb claim is a useful asset, but the 1m5f trip (13 furlongs) is beyond the 1m2f band of his best recent form.

runners_data.name: Kings Hill
runners_data.note: Paul Gilligan's seven-year-old has zero wins and four places on Good ground (0W4P) and his best efforts have come on Soft or Heavy — the Good going at Ballinrobe tonight is not his preferred surface and a 42-day absence adds an unknown, though he does hold stamina credentials from a 1m9f placing.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Gillian Scott's runner is a genuine prominent type by nature but has been pushed into a mapped midfield slot by the congestion of prominent horses in this field; his Good-ground record across 15 runs shows only one placing and no wins, making his redistribution-discounted chance hard to support regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Catherine Magennis
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners this four-year-old with just two runs on the card — a close second over 1m on Good and a seventh over 10f on Soft — and the tongue-tie is noted; the significant concern is whether a horse with so little experience gets the stamina test of 1m5f right, even if Carroll's tactical acumen is an asset.

runners_data.name: Nuit
runners_data.note: Colin Keane — a key booking — partners De Bromhead's four-year-old who has three placings from eleven Good-ground starts and a second over 12f at the Curragh; the tongue-tie is fitted and the 12-day turnaround is fresh enough, but stepping up from 14f to 13f today is a modest ask and Keane will likely deploy this hold-up type late.

runners_data.name: Pampar Lady
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, winning from the front over 18f on Soft in her last success, and Gavin Cromwell's seven-year-old has broad distance experience from 16f to 20f; Jack Kearney's 3lb claim reduces the weight to 127lbs and the STYLE_FIT flag reflects that in a field this prominent-heavy, sustaining the lead all the way is a harder ask than it looks — her role is king-maker as much as winner.

races.paceDynamic: Pampar Lady is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to press her hard from the gate over this 1m5f trip on Good ground at Ballinrobe, she should control fractions at a measured, sustainable pace. The field nominally contains several prominent-types — Catalani, Way Down South, and Highlander Addict — but the redistribution signals that Catalani and Way Down South are unlikely to secure their natural prominent berths, meaning Pampar Lady and Highlander Addict are most likely to actually sit close to the pace in practice, with Catherine Magennis also capable of tracking up. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, and Catalani and Way Down South in particular will be forced to settle in a more restrained position than is natural for them. A steady, uncontested gallop set by Pampar Lady over a staying distance on a flat track strongly favours hold-up runners with a sustained late run, particularly those proven at this trip and going — Black Heather and Nuit are the archetypal beneficiaries if the pace is kind to closers, though the controlled nature of the gallop also keeps prominent stalkers in the picture.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pampar Lady Controls, Closers Fire
scenarios.trigger: If Pampar Lady sets a steady uncontested tempo and the leaders hit the straight with reserves intact, allowing hold-up horses to deliver a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Pampar Lady dictates from the front at a measured gallop, leaving Black Heather and Nuit with enough pace to aim at coming off the final bend; the 1m5f trip rewards those ridden conservatively throughout. Hold-up profiles with proven Good-ground form at this distance are the primary beneficiaries of an uncontested, honest but not scorching pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Highlander Addict or Catherine Magennis tracks the leader close enough to pounce approaching the final furlong without getting swamped by late finishers.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third off Pampar Lady's controlled pace can produce a decisive move rounding the home turn and hold on before the hold-up brigade arrives; Highlander Addict's recent course-distance win on Good gives this real credibility. This shape suits those with tactical speed and a prominent racing position, not the redistributed types pushed back involuntarily.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Deep Closer Scores
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves genuinely taxing and the leaders tie up inside the final two furlongs, gifting a sweeping hold-up run.
scenarios.body: Should Pampar Lady misjudge the tempo or face unexpected early pressure and the front group overextend, Black Heather — who has shown strong late runs over similar trips on Good — has the profile to exploit a weakening lead. Figero also carries residual interest here given a good-ground win over this exact trip, though the fade-in-finish flag is a material concern.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Midfield Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the over-populated prominent group causes early jostling and disrupts the race shape, allowing a horse tracking from genuine midfield to benefit from the ensuing disorder.
scenarios.body: With Catalani and Way Down South forced into a midfield position that is not their natural home, either could make an uncharacteristic but opportunistic late move if the pace dynamic fragments; however, both are discounted here precisely because their STYLE_FIT flags confirm they are racing out of role. This is the lowest-probability shape and should only be considered if early reports confirm an unusually messy early gallop.

watchPoints.text: Pampar Lady's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the fulcrum of the race — if any prominent horse rushes up to harry her early, the entire pace map shifts and hold-up horses may not get the pace they need.

Catalani and Way Down South are both natural prominent horses mapped to midfield positions; watch to see whether Ben Coen or W J Lee attempt to push forward early, which could ignite a faster-than-expected early pace and dramatically change the shape.

Highlander Addict's trip concern is material — the switch from 1m2f to 1m5f is significant, and if Robyn Donaghue-Leahy pushes forward to get her natural position, the claim advantage could be neutralised by the extra ground late.

Figero's fade-in-finish flag combined with a 52-day absence makes his market position worth monitoring — if well-backed, there may be stable confidence that the layoff has addressed the fitness concern, but the form at this distance on Good ground does not strongly support his chances on face value.

Colin Keane's booking for Nuit is a notable positive in what looks a largely open maiden — track whether De Bromhead's runner drifts or firms in the market, as Keane rarely accepts mundane rides without expectation.
